findings.title: Height field source kernel has zero test coverage
findings.description: k_source_height (lines 360-417) implements height-field fluid sourcing with flat level, infinite back-fill, and bilinear-profile modes. None of the 14 test files exercise this kernel or the HeightSourceDesc codepath. The blender_background_acceptance.py test sets up sources but never enables height sourcing. The 13 validation tests only use SourceShapeDesc-based sources (box, sphere). All three back-modes (0=Infinite, 1=Flat, 2=Profile) are untested.
findings.impact: A broken or regressed height-field sourcing path would not be caught by the current test suite. This is a user-facing feature configured through FLUIDSIM_PT_sources panel, so a regression directly affects production simulations relying on height-wave tanks or infinite-ocean setups.
findings.fix: Add a validation test that enables height sourcing with base_height and emits particles, verifying voxel_type fluid bits are set below the height and absent above. Add a second test with a bilinear profile numpy array to validate the Profile back-mode interpolation.

findings.title: All 10 NanoVDB/OpenVDB volume sourcing kernels are untested
findings.description: Volume sourcing kernels (k_source_volume_float, k_source_volume_vector, k_source_volume_vector_component, k_source_volume_type_fog, k_source_volume_type_fog_with_temperature, k_source_volume_mask_fog, k_source_volume_type_sdf, k_source_volume_type_sdf_with_temperature, k_source_volume_mask_sdf, and two OpenVDB alias groups) have zero test coverage. These kernels sample wp.Volume (NanoVDB) grids to drive fluid sourcing, temperature, and masking. The test suite contains no wp.Volume construction or sampling.
findings.impact: Volume-based sourcing from NanoVDB/OpenVDB grids is completely uncovered. Any regression in volume sampling, coordinate transforms, blend modes, or fog threshold logic would go undetected until a user attempts to source from a VDB file.
findings.fix: Add validation tests that construct a small wp.Volume from a numpy array, attach it via the volume sourcing API, and verify fluid voxel marking, velocity/temperature attribution, and mask-bit setting. Use the coreSource* kernel registry names to target each path.

findings.title: Panel draw logic is completely uncovered by meaningful tests
findings.description: panels.py defines 13 FluidSim UI panels with complex conditional draw logic (enabled/disabled states, property visibility, dynamic labels dependent on session state and solver statistics). Current coverage is limited to registration checks: blender_background_acceptance.py and blender_gui_acceptance.py verify that hasattr(bpy.types, panel_id) succeeds. No test validates that draw() executes without error, that conditional enable/disable works, that dynamic labels render correctly, or that property edits through the panel have the intended effect. The snippet panel argument UI, diagnostics timer display, and validation results display rely on runtime data that no test populates meaningfully.
findings.impact: A Python error in any draw() method would crash Blender's UI for all panels, but the registration-only check would still pass. Users would see blank or broken panels with no test signal.
findings.fix: Add a panel draw smoke test that creates a full scene, initializes the solver, steps frames, and iterates every panel calling draw() with a real bpy.context, catching exceptions. Extend blender_gui_acceptance.py to verify each panel's draw produces expected label text under varied solver states (uninitialized, initialized, after step, after release).

findings.title: Operator error paths and failure modes have negligible coverage
findings.description: Of 17 operators, only the happy path is tested. Error branches remain uncovered: FLUIDSIM_OT_initialize (line 28) handles exceptions with CANCELLED but no test injects a failing initialization; FLUIDSIM_OT_step (line 80-84) auto-initializes on missing solver; FLUIDSIM_OT_reset (line 60) reports WARNING on inactive solver but no test verifies this; FLUIDSIM_OT_toggle_live (line 107) falls back to initialize_session but no test triggers this; FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_apply (line 433) returns CANCELLED on compile errors but no test injects invalid snippet code; FLUIDSIM_OT_inject_particles checks for uninitialized solver and missing active object but neither failure is tested.
findings.impact: Every operator has at least one uncovered CANCELLED path. A change that breaks error handling would pass the test suite. Users would see unhandled exceptions or incorrect status messages instead of graceful error reporting.
findings.fix: For each operator, write a test that triggers every CANCELLED path (e.g., call step without initializing, call inject_particles with no active object, call snippet_apply with invalid syntax, call export_frame after release) and assert the correct return code and status message.

findings.title: Three of four surface smoothing filters are untested
findings.description: surface.py defines four smoothing filters: dilate (k_smooth_surface_sdf_dilate, line 114), erode (k_smooth_surface_sdf_erode, line 144), box (line 176), and mean curvature flow (line 208). Validation test 9 (test_surface_sdf) only tests the box filter. The dilate, erode, and mean curvature flow kernels, which are selectable through the UI (surface_filter_type enum), have zero coverage.
findings.impact: A regression in the mean curvature flow SDF smoothing (the most complex filter with 19 stencil reads and mixed-derivative computation) or in the morphological dilate/erode operators would silently degrade surface quality but pass all current tests.
findings.fix: Extend test_surface_sdf in validation.py to create a known SDF landscape, apply each filter kernel, and verify expected signed-distance changes (e.g., dilate reduces negative region, erode expands it, mean curvature flow decreases surface area). Test the surface_filter_iterations loop with multiple passes.

findings.title: inject_particles method has no unit test coverage
findings.description: solver.FluidSolver.inject_particles (lines 1196-1227) is a public API that appends external particle arrays to the solver. It requires a k_source_particles kernel launch and proper particle attribute initialization. The only coverage comes indirectly through blender_background_acceptance.py which calls the inject_particles Blender operator, but that path goes through the Blender bridge, sources module, and viewport update, making it an integration test that can mask kernel-level failures.
findings.impact: A bug in the particle injection kernel launch parameters, attribute assignment, or capacity overflow handling would not be caught by any isolation test.
findings.fix: Add a unit-level validation test that creates a FluidSolver, calls inject_particles with a small set of known positions/velocities/temperatures, and reads back particle arrays to verify correct injection. Test the edge cases: empty array, velocity=None, use_lifespan=True, and capacity overflow.

findings.title: Pressure Jacobi solver path has inadequate isolation testing
findings.description: solve_jacobi (lines 905-925) is a public solver path selectable through the UI (pressure_solver = JACOBI). Validation test 8 (test_solver_convergence) calls ps.solve_pcg and ps.solve_jacobi sequentially on the same PressureSolver instance without resetting the RHS between calls, making the Jacobi result dependent on the preceding PCG state.
findings.impact: The Jacobi solver path is tested only in a contaminated state (residual already reduced by PCG). A regression specific to Jacobi could be masked because the starting residual is already low.
findings.fix: Create an isolated Jacobi test: build RHS from a known divergent velocity field on a fresh PressureSolver, call solve_jacobi alone, and measure residual reduction. Also test that pressure_iterations=1 produces a different result from pressure_iterations=100.

findings.title: CFL substep computation has no direct test coverage
findings.description: _compute_substeps (lines 1094-1112) calculates substeps per frame based on particle velocity, gravity, CFL number, and solver settings. It reads back max particle velocity from the GPU, introducing a sync point. The logic for max_speed_dev, gravity contribution, min/max substeps clamping, and the empty-particle-count early return are completely untested in isolation.
findings.impact: A regression in the CFL calculation could cause either too many substeps (performance regression) or too few (simulation instability/explosion). Neither would be caught by any existing assertion.
findings.fix: Write a focused test that creates a FluidSolver with known particle velocities, calls _compute_substeps with a fixed frame_dt, and asserts the returned substep count matches the expected CFL-based calculation. Test edge cases: zero particles, max_speed below threshold, gravity-only motion.

findings.title: Trilinear and MAC velocity sampling functions have no direct tests
findings.description: fields.py defines sample_scalar_trilinear, sample_mac_component, and sample_mac_velocity which are fundamental to G2P transfer, whitewater advection, and particle attribute sourcing. There are no unit-level tests that construct a known field, sample at known positions, and verify interpolated values against analytic expectations.
findings.impact: An off-by-one in the stencil offset, a sign error in the weight calculation, or a fallback value bug would silently produce incorrect interpolation across all subsystems that rely on field sampling.
findings.fix: Add a validation test that creates a small grid, sets a linear field, samples at multiple known positions (including voxel centers, faces, and edges), and compares against expected bilinear/trilinear values. Test sampling outside the allocated domain to verify fallback behavior.

findings.title: SparseGrid topology lifecycle methods have limited unit test coverage
findings.description: SparseGrid.begin_topology, mark_points, mark_world_box, expand, and finalize_topology (lines 425-491) are the core of adaptive grid management. Only the happy path is tested: a single mark_world_box call followed by finalize_topology. The expand iterations parameter, the overflow error path, and the leaf_table reconstruction after topology change are not tested in isolation.
findings.impact: A topology rebuild that incorrectly marks leaves, exceeds capacity silently, or corrupts the leaf_table would cause incorrect field access across the entire solver, manifesting as simulation artifacts or GPU crashes.
findings.fix: Write topology isolation tests: (1) mark two disjoint boxes and verify both sets of leaves are allocated; (2) call mark_points with particle arrays and verify matching leaf coverage; (3) call expand(0) and expand(2) and verify leaf ring counts differ; (4) verify that overflow raises RuntimeError.

findings.title: Particle lifecycle and sink check kernels have no isolated tests
findings.description: The k_particle_age, k_particle_lifespan, and k_particle_in_sink_check kernels that manage particle aging, lifespan expiration, and sink-based removal are exercised only through the full solver step_frame pipeline. No test verifies that particles are removed when they enter sink regions. The compact() method that follows lifecycle has no edge-case tests.
findings.impact: A regression in lifespan comparison, sink bit detection, or compaction indexing would silently cause particles to live forever, die prematurely, or corrupt the particle array.
findings.fix: Add tests for lifecycle: (1) create particles with known ages/lifespans, run lifecycle, verify expired particles are killed; (2) create a sink region via sourcing, place particles inside it, step, and verify particles are removed; (3) test compact() with all-dead, all-alive, and mixed particle populations.

findings.title: Particle compaction is never tested in isolation
findings.description: ParticleSystem.compact() (lines 121-154) performs GPU scan-based compaction. It has multiple internal operations: scan, scatter with k_compact_alive_scatter, buffer swap, and k_reset_alive re-mark. There are no tests for: compaction of an empty system, compaction where all particles are dead, compaction where no particles are dead, or the scan temporary buffer overflow behavior.
findings.impact: A bug in the exclusive scan, the scatter addressing, or the buffer swap logic would corrupt the particle array during every timestep.
findings.fix: Add direct tests for ParticleSystem.compact(): (1) seed particles with known alive/dead pattern, call compact, verify surviving prefix matches alive particles; (2) set count=0, call compact, verify count stays 0; (3) set all particles dead, compact, verify count=0.

findings.title: Source shape blend modes and shape primitives are under-tested
findings.description: Only SPHERE (validation test 5) and BOX (validation test 6) shapes are tested. The CYLINDER, PYRAMID, CONE, and PLANE shape primitives (shape_local_sdf lines 119-149) are never tested. The five blend modes (Add, Replace, Maximum, Pull, Blend) are only exercised with default mode=1 (Replace). The four force types (Directional, Omnidirectional, Spin, Radial) are not tested.
findings.impact: A regression in the signed-distance function for any untested shape primitive would not be caught. Users selecting those shapes would silently get incorrect emission regions.
findings.fix: Add validation tests that verify each shape primitive produces the correct approximate emission volume. Test blend modes by placing overlapping sources with different modes and verifying voxel-type and velocity field values.

findings.title: Particle relax kernel not tested in isolation
findings.description: The _relax() method (lines 982-1001) and k_particles_relax kernel perform particle separation-based relaxation. The relax_enabled, relax_strength, and relax_mode settings have no direct test coverage. The method re-indexes particles before relaxation, adding coupling between indexing and relaxation.
findings.impact: A regression in the particle relaxation kernel would degrade particle quality but current tests would not detect it. The only observable symptom would be visual clustering in the viewport.
findings.fix: Add a focused test that places particles in a highly non-uniform distribution, runs relaxation with known parameters, and measures the variance of particles per voxel before and after.

findings.title: Collision face and velocity expansion kernels not directly tested
findings.description: The _collision_faces() method (lines 859-876) uses k_sdf_to_axis_collision and k_expand_shift_axis_velocity_in_collider. No test validates that collision face bits are correctly set, that collider velocity is applied to the correct faces, or that velocity extrapolation into collision regions produces sensible values.
findings.impact: A bug in per-axis collision face marking would cause incorrect pressure boundary conditions, leading to fluid leaking through walls or bouncing off air.
findings.fix: Add validation tests: (1) create a known collision SDF, run k_sdf_to_axis_collision, verify correct VOXEL_COLLISION_* bits; (2) run k_expand_shift_axis_velocity_in_collider with known fluid velocities adjacent to a collision region and verify extrapolation.

findings.title: Particle scalar/vector field attribute sourcing kernels untested
findings.description: k_source_particle_scalar_field_attribute (line 509), k_source_particle_vector_field_attribute (line 534), k_source_particle_scalar_constant (line 566), and k_source_particle_integer_constant (line 585) sample grid fields into per-particle attributes at spawn time. None of these kernels have test coverage.
findings.impact: Particle attribute initialization from grid fields is completely uncovered. A regression in the trilinear sampling or attribute assignment logic would not be detected.
findings.fix: Add validation tests that create a grid with a known scalar field, spawn particles, and verify per-particle attributes match expected field values at their positions.

findings.title: Whitewater advection regime classification not validated
findings.description: k_advect_whitewater implements a three-regime advection model (foam/spray/bubble) based on surface SDF distance. Validation test 11 only checks that whitewater count > 0 and that particles remain inside the domain. It does not verify regime-specific behavior.
findings.impact: A regression that collapses all regimes to the same behavior or inverts the drag direction would not be caught.
findings.fix: Enhance validation test 11: sample particle velocities and positions and verify regime-appropriate properties (e.g., bubble particles have upward velocity, foam particles match fluid velocity, spray particles have ballistic arcs).

findings.title: Viscosity explicit smoothing path not tested in isolation
findings.description: ViscositySolver.smooth() (lines 293-308) implements explicit diffusion smoothing. Validation test 10 only tests the implicit PCG path. The Jacobi path within ViscositySolver._solve_component (lines 328-354) is also untested.
findings.impact: A regression in the explicit viscosity smoothing kernel would not be detected. Users selecting Jacobi viscosity would get incorrect diffusion behavior.
findings.fix: Add a test for ViscositySolver.smooth() with known velocity field and viscosity constant, verifying output velocities are averaged toward neighborhood means. Add a test with use_pcg=False to exercise the Jacobi path.

findings.title: Custom snippet compilation and execution not unit-tested
findings.description: The SnippetManager is exercised only through blender_background_acceptance.py integration test. There are no tests for syntax errors, runtime errors, FIELD_ACCESSORS for all 17 fields, argument binding with FIELD and CONSTANT modes, multiple snippets at the same hook, or all 5 hook points.
findings.impact: The custom kernel snippet system is a key differentiator. A regression in code generation, field binding, or hook placement would break user-written custom physics without warning.
findings.fix: Add validation tests: (1) compile snippet with syntax error and verify error reporting; (2) compile snippet writing to each accessible field and verify field change; (3) compile snippets at each hook order and verify execution.

findings.title: Mesh collision velocity kernel has no test coverage
findings.description: k_mesh_collision_velocity (lines 158-188) and k_create_sdf_from_mesh_axis compute collision velocities from animated mesh colliders. No test creates a mesh collider with non-zero velocity and verifies the resulting collision_vel array.
findings.impact: Animated mesh colliders with transfer_velocity enabled have no automated test coverage. A regression would go undetected.
findings.fix: Add a validation test that creates a warp.Mesh, constructs a FluidSolver with a ColliderDesc referencing the mesh with non-zero linear_velocity, steps the solver, and verifies collision_vel values near the collider match prescribed motion.

findings.title: Domain SDF wall marking has no test coverage
findings.description: k_mark_domain_walls enforces closed-domain boundary conditions when domain_sdf_walls=True and open_boundaries=False. No test enables these settings. The default is False for both, making this feature effectively dead code with zero coverage.
findings.impact: Users who enable domain SDF walls would rely on a completely untested feature. A regression could cause fluid to leak through domain boundaries.
findings.fix: Add a validation test that sets domain_sdf_walls=True, open_boundaries=False, creates a solver with fluid near the boundary, steps, and verifies collision SDF values at domain walls are negative.

findings.title: Speed limit force kernel not tested
findings.description: k_forces_speed_limit is launched when settings.max_speed > 0. The speed_limit_behavior and speed_limit_percent parameters are complex and completely uncovered.
findings.impact: Users who enable speed limiting get no test coverage. A regression that disables clamping would not be caught.
findings.fix: Add a validation test that sets max_speed to a small value, introduces particles with velocities exceeding the limit, steps the solver, and verifies velocities are clamped. Test both speed_limit_behavior modes.

findings.title: Solver step_frame pipeline phases lack individual phase verification
findings.description: step_frame() orchestrates 15+ phases per substep. Tests only verify aggregate outcomes: particle count > threshold, surface mesh non-empty. Individual phase contributions are never verified.
findings.impact: A phase that silently produces no effect would not be detected because only the cumulative effect is checked.
findings.fix: Extract individual phases and verify postconditions (e.g., after _forces measure velocity change; after _surface verify SDF negative inside particle cloud). Add FrameStats timer range assertions.

findings.title: Pressure multigrid coarse initial guess path not validated for accuracy
findings.description: coarse_initial_guess() computes a per-leaf electrostatic potential as a long-range initial guess for PCG. The default SolverSettings has pressure_multigrid=OFF, so this path is never tested. The k_build_leaf_aggregates, k_solve_leaf_potential_jacobi, k_sample_up_leaf_potential, and k_sample_down_residual kernels have zero coverage.
findings.impact: The multigrid acceleration for pressure solving is completely untested. A regression would only manifest as slower simulation, which no test measures.
findings.fix: Add a test that solves with pressure_multigrid=OFF (baseline), then with VCycle, and verifies the V-cycle reduces PCG iterations to reach the same residual.

findings.title: PCG failure status test does not verify all failure paths
findings.description: test_pcg_reports_failure_status_when_system_cannot_converge creates a system with all collision voxels and expects PCG to fail. It accepts any of four reasons as valid, which is overly permissive. Each failure mode should have a dedicated test.
findings.impact: A change that silently converts one failure mode to another would not be detected. Each failure path in the PCG loop has distinct diagnostic value.
findings.fix: Create separate pytest functions for each failure mode: singular system, stalled, non-finite RHS, max_iterations. Each should verify the precise status string.

findings.title: Validation subset runner has no self-tests for indexing correctness
findings.description: _subset_runner.py runs a subset of validation tests by index into _TESTS. There are no tests that verify the index-to-name mapping is correct. A developer adding a new validation test could insert it at the wrong position and silently shift all subsequent index references.
findings.impact: An off-by-one in the index mapping would cause the wrong validation tests to run under a given test file name, creating a false sense of coverage.
findings.fix: Add a self-verification test that runs all 13 validation tests by name lookup and asserts the subset runner indices map to the correct validation_name strings.

findings.title: smoke_core.py is an ad-hoc script not a proper test
findings.description: smoke_core.py (48 lines) is a standalone script with no assertions, no test framework integration, and no error handling. It hardcodes device cuda:0 with no fallback. It overlaps substantially with validation tests 1-3 and 7-8 but without structured pass/fail criteria.
findings.impact: This file provides limited value as a test because it has no pass/fail criteria besides not crashing.
findings.fix: Migrate unique coverage into a new validation test in validation.py. Remove hardcoded device string in favor of a configurable parameter.

findings.title: Output accessor methods have minimal coverage
findings.description: surface_mesh(), particle_positions(), particle_velocities(), and whitewater_positions() (lines 1231-1251) are the primary output accessors. Only surface_mesh() and particle_positions() are tested in smoke_solver.py. particle_velocities() and whitewater_positions() are not directly tested.
findings.impact: A regression in host-to-device transfer for velocity or whitewater position retrieval would silently produce empty or corrupted data for viewport display and export.
findings.fix: Add tests that call each output accessor after a few steps, verifying correct dtype, shape, and approximate value ranges. Test the zero-particle edge case for each.

findings.title: GUI acceptance test relies on real wall-clock timing, making it flaky
findings.description: blender_gui_acceptance.py uses a timer-driven state machine with fixed wall-clock delays (3.0 seconds for playback, 0.2 seconds for UI phase) rather than checking for state readiness. On slower GPUs the 3-second window may be insufficient. On fast GPUs, the test wastes time waiting.
findings.impact: The test may produce non-deterministic failures in CI environments with variable GPU availability.
findings.fix: Replace fixed-delay phases with readiness-polling: poll sess.solver.frame until it reaches the expected count or a timeout expires.

findings.title: Validation tests lack coverage of rendering and export paths
findings.description: The 13 validation tests do not exercise the rendering viewport bridge, Blender materials, export (obj/ply) writer, or cache system. The export module (io/export.py) and cache module (io/cache.py) have no unit tests at all.
findings.impact: Changes to export or cache subsystems have no fast feedback. A regression would only be caught by the full Blender acceptance test, which is slow.
findings.fix: Add lightweight tests that construct a solver, run frames, and call the export function directly, verifying .obj and .ply files with correct vertex counts. Test cache round-trip: save state, reload, compare.

findings.title: Whitewater compaction has no isolation test
findings.description: WhitewaterSystem.compact() (lines 373-414) uses a scan-based compaction with helper kernels k_ww_compact_scatter, k_ww_final_count, k_ww_mark_alive. It refreshes host count before compaction and slices arrays by current count. There are no direct tests.
findings.impact: A bug in whitewater compaction could silently corrupt the whitewater particle array every frame.
findings.fix: Add a focused test: seed whitewater particles with known alive/dead pattern, call compact, verify count and particle data. Test edge cases: zero particles, all dead, capacity boundary.
